title: AMIP SST step corrections reduce the 1982-2022 radiation-curvature gap by 5-44% in five linear models
abstract: We tested how known SST steps change quadratic curvature of the net radiation response in five linear atmosphere-model Green functions. We used verified monthly projections for PCMDI-AMIP 1.1.9 and the OI2p1 1.0 prototype on a common ice-free ocean mask. In 1982-2022, the five-model mean new-minus-old curvature gap is -0.06672 W m-2 per decade squared. Forty correction pairs reduce its size by 5-44%, but leave a negative gap. In 2001-2022 the gap is positive, and corrections can reduce it by 16% or increase it by 23%. The 2005 and 2020 events have large opposing short-period effects. We also construct curvature weights that remove arbitrary offsets at the known event dates. These weights retain 56-61% of independent-noise curvature information in 1982-2022 and 26-36% in 2001-2022. All tested corrections leave their estimates unchanged. Long-period individual curvature intervals include zero under the tested residual model. These results concern linear SST-induced radiation only. They do not test observed energy-imbalance acceleration. Correction maps, event shapes, smooth bias and model response remain uncertain. The package contains the input aggregates, code, weights, tables, figures, provenance and independent checks.
